packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-23 - unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure: nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading of this fragment. The only external text seen is a modern pencil shelfmark note on the strip itself (see below).

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, overview, face 1)
- A single narrow horizontal paper(?)/parchment strip, c. 13.5 x 1.7 cm by the scale, held by two spatulas, on black ground with colour chart and ruler.
- Orientation: text upright, running left to right along the length of the strip.
- Three complete written lines plus the cut-off descenders/lower parts of a fourth line above (top edge trims through it). Bottom edge trims close under line 3.
- Single block of text, no columns visible; left part of the strip has a blank margin carrying a modern pencil note in three lines: "Stams, / StA, Fr. / 44r" (archive/shelfmark note, not part of the text). A faint horizontal line (fold or ruling?) runs through the left margin area.
- Script: German-language cursive (Kurrent-type chancery/letter hand), brown ink. No rubrics, initials, underlining or glosses visible. Text is cut at the right edge (words run off).
- Tentative: vernacular German prose, possibly a letter or document; no inference beyond that.

Pencil note in left margin (modern, not text): image-002.jpg: "Stams, / STA, Fr?. (reads like "Fig." / "Frg.") / 44r".

TRANSCRIPTION, face 1 (image-001 overview; tiles image-002 = left half, image-003 = right half; they overlap in the middle)
Line numbering: L0 = the trimmed line at the top (only descenders/ascender tips visible), L1-L3 full lines.

image-002.jpg (left half; crop-01.jpg = contrast-enhanced enlargement of its text area)
002 L0: only the foot of one tall stroke (l/h/long s?) and a hook near the right, above "Vogtl"; [illegible, trimmed]
002 L1: auff vmb(?) [or vnd] der V?gtl(?) [cap. V/B + o/a + g/s? + t + l; "Vogtl"? "Vastl"?] gip... [continues on image-003]
002 L2: daraus(?) [first letter a looped d/D; word could be "daran"/"darans"] (?)schreibt(?) [word opens with a looped stroke, reads ?-schri/fri-...-tl; very uncertain] vnd von(?) [or "vns"/"vnd"] ... [continues]
002 L3: der Vnater(?) [or "Vnnter"? "Vater" with extra minim?] ar(?)/an(?) diss?(?) [d/c + i + long-s ligature, "dissz"?] belenth(?)/beledt(?) ... [continues]
Note: L2 has a stain/blot crossing between "vnd" and the L3 word "diss?".

image-003.jpg (right half; overlaps image-002 from "V?gtl" (L1) / "vnd von" (L2) / "belenth" (L3); crop-02.jpg = contrast-enhanced view of the whole tile)
003 L0: tails of several letters (ascender/descender loops, an "f/s"-like hook, a "p"-like bowl) cut by the top edge; [illegible, trimmed]
003 L1: [V?gt]l(?) geschickt(?) [g + e + long s/ph + c + h + i + c + k + t; could be "gephickt"] vnd genugsamblich(?) [g + e/m-minims + u + g + long s + a + m + (b?) + l + i + c + h; alt. "gemainsamlich"] mit d... [cut at right edge]
003 L2: vnd von(?) Hanz(?) [or "Hanns"/"Hainz"] Hayim(?) [H + a + y(with diaeresis-like dots) + i? + m/n; "Hayim"/"Hajen"?] gesetzt(?) [or "geprobt"/"geschickt"? g + e + s/p + e? + z + t] / er schickt d... [virgule "/" before "er"; final word cut at right edge]
003 L3: [ ... ] belenth(?) [or "belanth"/"beledt"; final letter has a long looped tail, perhaps a closing bracket ")"] ich habe(?) [h + a + b + e/o] auch(?) [a + u/v + c? + h with long flourish] nit so hoch an... [cut at right edge; "so" begins with a looped long s]

Running text as read (overlap merged, uncertain words marked):
L1: auff vmb(?) der V?gtl(?) geschickt(?) vnd genugsamblich(?) mit d[...]
L2: daraus(?) (?)schreibt(?) vnd von(?) Hanz(?) Hayim(?) gesetzt(?) / er schickt d[...]
L3: der Vnater(?) an(?) diss?(?) belenth(?) ich habe(?) auch(?) nit so hoch an[...]

Selected/unread: face 1 read in full (3 lines); L0 and right-edge continuations are lost to trimming.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-004.jpg, overview, face 2)
- The same strip, other face. A uniform grey rectangle (digital mask, not part of the object) covers the upper-left two-thirds of the strip in the overview and in tiles image-005 (left) and image-006 (left part). Whatever lies under it cannot be read.
- Visible parts (lower band of the strip throughout; full height at the right third): no medieval/early-modern script visible, only paper/parchment surface with creases, a dark stain at upper right (image-006, near right edge) and a small dark mark at the bottom right corner (spatula/shadow?).
- Modern pencil note, image-006 bottom centre: "Stams, StA, Frg. 44v". (This confirms the margin note on face 1 reads "Frg." = 44r.)

TRANSCRIPTION, face 2
image-005.jpg: no text visible outside the grey mask.
image-006.jpg: no text visible outside the grey mask apart from the pencil shelfmark above. A faint brownish smudge at the top right (image-006, c. x 1440-1480, y 200-250) is a stain, not legible writing.

LIMITATIONS
- Face 1: strip trimmed top and bottom and at the right edge; only three full lines survive, each cut off mid-word at the right. Fast cursive German hand with heavy loops; several word readings (esp. L1 word 4, L2 words 2 and 6, L3 words 2-4) are tentative. Personal names in L2 ("Hanz Hayim"?) are especially uncertain.
- Face 2: largely obscured by a digital grey mask in all three images; unread beneath it.
- Crops made: crop-01.jpg (image-002 text area, greyscale, autocontrast, 1.8x), crop-02.jpg (image-003, greyscale, autocontrast, 1.2x).
- Nothing done beyond the brief, except that a directory listing of the packet folder showed the filename packet.json (not opened).
